outcome: Yuhang Zhao's arXiv preprint 2603.20890 (21 Mar 2026) improves the Choi-Wang lower bound on the first eigenvalue, leaving Yau's conjecture open; Zeng's 2025 claimed full proof is set aside as not credible. [Judged 2026-09-28; the researcher's original outcome follows.] Lingzhong Zeng posted a single-author arXiv preprint (2508.06123, 8 Aug 2025) claiming a full, affirmative proof of Yau's conjecture, but over a year later it remains an unreviewed single version (v1), has drawn no visible citations, expert commentary, or journal acceptance, and later 2026 preprints on the identical question (e.g. 2606.10962, June 2026) still describe the conjecture as open and do not cite or engage with Zeng's claim — so the claim has not been digested by experts and does not warrant `resolved`.
summary: The triage correctly flagged Lingzhong Zeng's arXiv preprint 2508.06123 ("The First Eigenvalue of Embedded Minimal Hypersurfaces in the Unit Sphere I: Yau's Conjecture", submitted 8 Aug 2025) as claiming a full proof that the first non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on any embedded compact minimal hypersurface of the unit sphere S^{n+1} equals n, via a minimizing sequence in a suitable Sobolev space and the variational principle, with rigidity theorems as applications. I fetched the abstract and full text directly: it is a genuine claim to resolve the conjecture as stated, not a restricted case or a variant, so it is squarely in scope under §3.1. However, it carries only one arXiv version (v1, unchanged since posting, comment field reads only 'Any comment is welcome'), no journal reference, and I could find no citing papers, no MathOverflow/blog/expert discussion, and no acknowledgement of it anywhere. Critically, two later 2026 preprints on the exact same narrow topic — Yuhang Zhao's arXiv:2603.20890 (21 Mar 2026, improving the Choi-Wang bound on the same eigenvalue problem) and an anonymous-to-me author's arXiv:2606.10962 (10 Jun 2026, 'On the First Eigenvalue of Embedded Minimal Hypersurfaces in the Unit Sphere', giving an improved partial lower bound) — both still frame Yau's conjecture as an open problem and neither cites nor mentions Zeng's claimed resolution at all. That silence from directly adjacent, contemporaneous work is strong indirect evidence the field either has not noticed the claim or does not regard it as settling the question. Per §6.1, a preprint with no expert digestion is `claimed`, not `resolved`, however clean the argument looks on the page — and here there is additionally a live signal (continued 'open' framing by close successors) suggesting doubt rather than mere lag. I found no AI involvement anywhere: Zeng's paper is a traditional single-author variational-methods argument with no mention of AI/ML/computational assistance, and the two 2026 follow-up papers likewise show no AI involvement. Wikipedia's own article on the conjecture (last substantively updated before Zeng's preprint) still calls it unsolved, consistent with the frozen revision's framing, and is not itself evidence either way about the post-cutoff period.
competing_reading: One could argue Zeng's is a serious, detailed single-author proof by an established researcher in this exact subfield (he has prior papers on partial results toward this same conjecture going back over a decade), and that arXiv preprints in this area sometimes go uncited for a year before slower-moving referees catch up — in which case `claimed` might understate confidence that the proof is probably correct. But the silence from Zhao (Mar 2026) and the Jun 2026 paper, both narrowly on-topic, tips this toward genuine non-acceptance or at least non-notice rather than mere citation lag, so I did not upgrade to `resolved`.
what_would_settle_it: A citation, review, or explicit endorsement/refutation of Zeng's 2508.06123 by another expert in minimal-surface spectral geometry (e.g., in a paper, MathOverflow thread, or Tao/Matroid-Union-style digestion), or a journal acceptance record for that preprint, or an explicit statement in a later preprint that the conjecture is now considered proved (or that Zeng's argument has a gap).

events.what: Zeng claims a full affirmative proof that the first eigenvalue on any embedded minimal hypersurface of S^{n+1} is n
events.credibility_reason: F5: landmark problem, over a year with no citations, commentary or acceptance; two later preprints bounding exactly this eigenvalue (2603.20890, Mar 2026; 2606.10962, Jun 2026) still call the conjecture open and do not cite the claim; a full proof via a minimizing sequence and the variational principle is a method this long-open problem is not expected to yield to so simply. Counterweight: the author has prior work in the area, so this is a judgement call, but same-topic silence is as close to a knock-down as silence gets.
